title: Scalar transport for inverse-image module stalks on ringed spaces
statement: For ringed spaces X,Y, a continuous map f:X→Y, alpha:inverseImageRing f OY→OX, and x in X, let k:OY_(f x)→(inverseImageRing f OY)_x be stalkPullbackHom followed by the stalk of sheafification, psi = alpha_x, and rho = psi k. There exist natural additive isomorphisms c_M:M_(f x)≃(inverseImageModule f OY M)_x and OX_x-linear isomorphisms beta_M:extendScalars rho M_(f x)≅extendScalars psi (inverseImageModule f OY M)_x with beta_M(b tensor m)=b tensor c_M(m). Naturality means c_N(a_(f x)(m))=(inverseImageModuleMap a)_x(c_M(m)). Stalks and inverse images use [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module], and [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. No complexes or changed sheaf stalks are involved.

source.place: Tag 0098, proof of lemma-stalk-pullback-modules using inverse-image stalks (Tag 008H).

proof.text: Identify the constructed inverse image with the chosen topological sheaf pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints. Apply the inverse-image stalk comparisons for rings and abelian groups, with their unit germ formulas. Equivalently, compute the constructed comparison as stalkPullbackHom followed by stalk of sheafification. This gives the ring isomorphism k and natural additive isomorphisms c.

Represent a scalar and a module element on a common open neighborhood. The germ formulas for the ring and abelian units, together with semilinearity of the chosen inverseImageModuleInstances unit, give c_M(r m)=k(r)c_M(m). Naturality of the inverse-image abelian comparison identifies its maps with stalkAddMap of inverseImageModuleMap.

Construct beta on pure tensors by b tensor m ↦ b tensor c_M(m). The relation c_M(r m)=k(r)c_M(m) and rho=psi k prove balancing. Construct the inverse by b tensor n ↦ b tensor c_M inverse(n); inverse semilinearity and rho(k inverse(s))=psi(s) prove its balancing. Both are OX_x-linear and both composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all tensors. This proves the beta formula. The preceding naturality proves the last clause.

theorem exists_ringed_inverseImage_stalk_scalar_transport
    (X Y : RingedSpace.{u}) (f : X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier)
    (α : TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f Y.sheaf ⟶ X.sheaf) (x : X) :
    let k := TopCat.Presheaf.stalkPullbackHom CommRingCat.{u} f Y.presheaf x ≫
      (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat.{u} x).map
        (toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          ((TopCat.Presheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).obj Y.presheaf))
    let ψ : TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X.carrier)
        (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f Y.sheaf).obj x →+* X.presheaf.stalk x :=
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat.{u} x).map α.hom).hom
    let ρ := ψ.comp k.hom
    ∃ (c : ∀ M : RingedSpace.Modules Y,
        (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).obj M ≃+
          TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X.carrier)
            (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModule f Y.sheaf M).val.presheaf x)
      (β : ∀ M : RingedSpace.Modules Y,
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars ρ).obj
            ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).obj M) ≅
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars ψ).obj
            (ModuleCat.of (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u})
              (X := X.carrier) (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f Y.sheaf).obj x)
              (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X.carrier)
                (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModule f Y.sheaf M).val.presheaf x))),
      (∀ (M : RingedSpace.Modules Y) (b : X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (m : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).obj M),
        (β M).hom (b ⊗ₜ[_, ρ] m) = b ⊗ₜ[_, ψ] (c M m)) ∧
      (∀ (M N : RingedSpace.Modules Y) (a : M ⟶ N)
        (m : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).obj M),
        c N ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).map a m) =
          PresheafOfModules.stalkAddMap
            (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModuleMap f Y.sheaf M a).val (c M m))
